title: The Triad of Civilization: Matter · Energy · Intent
subtitle: Beyond E = mc²: The Geometry of Semantic Realization and Thermodynamic Control

blocks.text: This chapter presents the poster “The Triad of Civilization: Matter · Energy · Intent” in full. It is a single dense diagram; open it, then use the explanation, read-aloud, and Ask-AI tools beneath it to work through the ideas at your own pace.

blocks.explanation: The framework's foundational physics of civilization. Matter is what can exist physically and sets the structural boundary conditions; energy is what enables change and sets the rate and scale of realization; intent is what determines purpose and sets the directional vector. The poster's central claim about E = mc² is that mass-energy equivalence tells you how much energy can be liberated from matter but carries no information about why or where that energy should be directed — intent supplies the missing top-down geometric constraint. The thermodynamic inversion panel is the argument's sharpest edge: matter and energy operate at collective scale and enormous capital intensity, while intent operates at individual scale and minimal capital intensity, so a single verified ontology, formal proof or intent specification authored by one mind can reorganize vast quantities of matter and energy. The remaining panels give civilizational homeostasis as a dynamic equilibrium of the three, the failure modes when any one is absent, and the Zistgah habitat continuum from Earth through Mars and the Moon to future worlds, each a nested Markov blanket.
blocks.tts: The triad of civilization: matter, energy and intent. Matter builds, energy moves, intent means. As civilization evolves, the capital intensity of power inverts — and purpose precedes execution.
